newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's PCS sees "substantially lower" profits.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's PCS sees "substantially lower" profits.

text.p: The Petrochemical Corporation of Singapore (PCS) expects 1996 profits to be substantially lower than in 1995 due to falling product prices, company managing director Takayuki Okada said on Friday.
"1996 profit will be substantially lower than 1995," Okada told a news conference.
He declined to give any indication of how large the reduction in profits would be. In 1995 PCS profits soared to Singapore $92.6 million from $71.1 million in 1994.
Its earnings sank to a low of $16.2 million in 1993 when the industry was in the depth of its most recent cyclical bust year.
The company is a 50:50 joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and a consortium of Japanese companies.
Okada told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that prices would come under pressure in the next two to three years and as a result company profitability will also be affected.
But he said he was confident that "PCS and our Complex will continue to hold a very competitive market position in this region to weather any volatility in the market."

The company is expanding its ethylene production by 515,000 tonnes per year. Ethylene is at the heart of a S$3.4 billion petrochemical complex is expected to start up early in the second quarter of 1997.

The Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Friday that petrochemical output for the year fell by 10.5 percent in dollar terms despite a 6.0 percent increase in production volume, "mainly due to sluggish product prices."
"Prices of key petrochemicals such as polyolefins and paraxylene fell by 10-20 percent globally compared to 1995, resulting in weak margins," the EDB said in a statement.
Polyolefins such as polyethylene and polypropylene are downstream products which use the ethylene and propylene produced by PCS.
PCS currently operates a 450,000 tonne per year ethylene plant at Pulau Ayer Merbau, one of a group of small islands off the southern coast of Singapore.
